### 1.3 Key Observations

1. **Eurex Clearing has the largest aggregate CCP/parent financial commitment** at EUR 1.7 billion (including the Deutsche Borse Letter of Comfort), providing the most comprehensive loss-absorbing capacity beyond participant resources.

2. **ASX has the most unique SITG model**: ASX Clear's cash equities default fund is 100% funded by the CCP itself (AUD 250M), and ASX Clear (Futures) contributes 69% of the total default fund (AUD 450M of AUD 650M). This reflects the vertically integrated ownership model.

3. **ICE introduced innovation** with its default insurance layer (renewed for three-year terms), which adds $200M across its clearing houses between SITG and non-defaulting members' contributions. Aggregate ICE SITG + insurance exceeds $660M.

4. **CME places distinct SITG amounts** in its Base ($100M) and IRS ($150M) waterfalls, totaling $250M in pre-funded own resources.

5. **U.S. user-owned CCPs (NSCC, OCC)** have relatively smaller SITG amounts (estimated $25-76M), reflecting their cooperative ownership models where participants bear the primary mutualized risk.

6. **HKEX uses a fixed-percentage model** (10% of fund size) for its SITG across all three clearing houses, providing simplicity and proportionality.

7. **Cover 2 is the predominant standard** for systemically important CCPs (LCH, OCC, CME, Eurex, JSCC, HKEX), while Cover 1 is used by some smaller or less systemic CCPs.

## 2. Margin Methodology Comparison

### 2.1 Summary Table

| CCP | Methodology | Risk Measure | Confidence Level | Lookback Period | Holding Period (ETD) | Holding Period (OTC) | Anti-Procyclicality | Cross-Margining |
|-----|-------------|-------------|-----------------|-----------------|---------------------|---------------------|--------------------|-----------------|
| **NSCC** | Parametric VaR | VaR | 99% | Historical price data | 3-day MPOR | N/A | Anti-cyclical charges | Cross-guaranty with FICC, OCC |
| **FICC-GSD** | Historical simulation VaR | VaR | Cover 1 target | Historical data | 3-day liquidation | N/A | Volatility Event Charge | Cross-margining with CME |
| **LCH** (SwapClear) | PAIRS (ES based on FHS with vol scaling) | Expected Shortfall | 99.7% | 10 years (with GFC window) | N/A | 5 days (members); 7 days (clients) | Stress period floor (unscaled 10-yr + 2.5-yr GFC) | Within SwapClear service |
| **LCH** (CDSClear) | HS with scaled returns, ES | Expected Shortfall | 99.7% | From April 2007 | N/A | 5 days | [data not available] | Within CDSClear service |
| **OCC** | STANS (Monte Carlo simulation) | Expected Shortfall | 99% ES (99.5% for top 2 sub-portfolios) | Historical data (dynamic) | 2 days | N/A | Floor based on historical averages | Cross-margin with CME (equity index options vs futures) |
| **CME** (Legacy SPAN) | 16 parametric scenarios | Worst-case loss | ~99% | Static parameter updates | 1 day | 5 days (OTC IRS) | APC measures | Cross-margin with OCC and FICC |
| **CME** (SPAN 2) | Historical VaR + ES | HVaR + ES | 99.7%+ [unverified] | Historical data (dynamic) | 1 day | 5 days | Anti-procyclical features | Cross-margin with OCC and FICC |
| **Eurex** (Prisma) | Filtered Historical Simulation VaR | Max of FHS-VaR and stress-period VaR | 99% (listed); 99.5% (OTC) | 3 years (750 scenarios) + stress period (250 scenarios) | 2-3 days | 5 days | Stress period VaR floor; annual recalibration | Listed-OTC cross-margining within PFI01 (up to 70% savings) |
| **JSCC** (Listed) | Historical Simulation VaR + Alternative Simulation VaR | VaR | 99%+ | 1,250+ data points | 1-2 days | N/A | [data not available] | Cross-margin between IRS and listed derivatives (TONA futures, JGB futures) |
| **JSCC** (IRS) | Historical Simulation ES | Expected Shortfall | Average of worst 1% | 1,250 business days | N/A | 5 days (house); 7 days (client) | [data not available] | Cross-margin with listed derivatives |
| **HKSCC** | VaR-based portfolio margining (Tier P); flat-rate (Tier N) | VaR | [data not available] | [data not available] | Settlement exposure (T+2) | N/A | [data not available] | No |
| **HKCC/SEOCH** | PRiME (SPAN 1-compatible; 16 scenarios) | Worst-case loss | Calibrated | [data not available] | 1 day | N/A | [data not available] | No |
| **CDP** | Risk-based VaR | VaR | 99% | [data not available] | 1-5 days | N/A | [data not available] | No |
| **Cboe Clear Europe** | Historical simulation CVaR | CVaR | 99% | 700 scenarios (~2.8 years) | 2 days | N/A | Stressed Historical Simulation (StressHS) | Cross-product margining (equities, derivatives, SFT) |
| **ICE** (IRM 1) | Scenario-based (SPAN-like) | Worst-case loss | [data not available] | Static parameters | 1 day | N/A | Limited | Within product segments |
| **ICE** (IRM 2) | Filtered Historical Simulation VaR | FHS-VaR | [data not available] | Historical data (dynamic) | 1 day | N/A | Built-in anti-procyclical features | Portfolio-level |
| **ASX Clear** (Cash) | Filtered Historical Simulation VaR | FHSVaR | High confidence | Historical data | Settlement exposure | N/A | [data not available] | No |
| **ASX Clear (Futures)** | CME SPAN | Worst-case loss | 3 std dev of 60-day distribution | Multiple lookback periods (7d, 120d, 12m) | 1 day | 5 days (OTC) | [data not available] | Within SPAN product groups |
| **KRX** | KRX-SPAN (modified SPAN) | Worst-case loss | Not disclosed | Historical data | 1 day | N/A | Intraday margin at KOSPI 200 volatility ≥80% | Within KRX derivatives |

### 2.2 Methodology Deep-Dive

**SPAN (CME Legacy / HKCC PRiME / ASX Clear (Futures))**
- Evaluates 16 hypothetical risk scenarios combining price and volatility shifts
- Calculates worst-case loss within each combined commodity group
- Adds intra-commodity spread charges and subtracts inter-commodity spread credits
- Transparent and widely adopted (50+ exchanges globally), but limited by its parametric nature and inability to capture tail risk dynamically
- Being replaced by SPAN 2 at CME; JSCC migrated away from SPAN to VaR in November 2023

**PRISMA / FHS (Eurex)**
- 750 filtered historical scenarios + 250 stress period scenarios = 1,000 total
- Volatility filtering ensures model reactivity to changing conditions
- Forward-looking stress period VaR floor prevents margin erosion during calm periods
- Cross-margining between listed fixed income (2-day HP) and OTC IRS (5-day HP) within PFI01 liquidation group -- unique feature delivering up to 70% margin savings
- Annual margin floor recalibration (e.g., Prisma Release 15.0 effective June 2025)

**PAIRS (LCH)**
- Expected Shortfall (ES) at 99.7% confidence -- highest confidence level among major CCPs
- 10-year lookback with volatility scaling (EWMA-based) to reflect current conditions
- Floor calibrated using unscaled 10-year lookback plus 2.5-year GFC window
- Member MPOR of 5 days for SwapClear, 7 days for client clearing (additional 2 days for portfolio transfer)
- Proven in managing the Lehman Brothers default (2008): used only 35% of Lehman's IM for a $9 trillion portfolio

**STANS (OCC)**
- World's first large-scale Monte Carlo-based margin methodology for derivatives clearing (2006)
- 99% Expected Shortfall with enhanced 99.5% ES for the two largest sub-portfolio exposures
- 2-day holding period (longer than CME's 1-day for comparable products)
- Full portfolio margining capturing non-linearities, correlations, and tail risk
- Being enhanced to address 0DTE option risks (Intraday Risk Charge approved April 2025)

**IRM 2 (ICE)**
- Next-generation Filtered Historical Simulation VaR replacing scenario-based IRM 1
- Portfolio-level risk assessment capturing all relationships and diversifying effects
- Built-in anti-procyclical features and seasonality adjustment
- Phased rollout: live for ICE Clear U.S. equity index futures (Jan 2022), ICE Clear Europe freight and energy (Sep-Nov 2025), remaining products TBD

**VaR-based approaches (JSCC, HKSCC, CDP, Cboe Clear Europe)**
- JSCC migrated from SPAN to VaR (November 2023) using dual HS-VaR and AS-VaR methods, with 1,250+ data points -- a major modernization aligning with global trends
- Cboe Clear Europe uses CVaR with 700 historical scenarios and real-time recalculation every 5 minutes
- HKSCC uses VaR for large/mid-cap securities (Tier P) but flat-rate margins for smaller securities (Tier N)

### 2.3 Key Observations

1. **Global convergence toward VaR/ES models**: SPAN is being phased out in favor of historical simulation VaR and Expected Shortfall approaches. CME (SPAN 2), JSCC (VaR), and ICE (IRM 2) have all migrated or are migrating away from parametric scenario-based methods.

2. **LCH operates at the highest confidence level** (99.7% ES with PAIRS), reflecting the systemic importance and complexity of OTC IRS clearing.

3. **Eurex Prisma offers the most advanced cross-margining**, enabling margin offsets between listed and OTC products within the same liquidation group -- a capability most other CCPs lack.

4. **Holding periods vary significantly**: 1 day (CME ETD, ICE ETD), 2 days (OCC, Eurex listed, Cboe Clear Europe), 3 days (NSCC), 5 days (OTC products at LCH, CME, Eurex, JSCC, ASX).

5. **Anti-procyclicality measures are increasingly mandated**: Eurex uses stress period VaR floors; Cboe Clear Europe uses Stressed Historical Simulation; CME SPAN 2 incorporates built-in anti-procyclical features. EMIR explicitly requires CCPs to implement anti-procyclicality tools.

### 3.2 T+1 Transition Status

| Market | Current | T+1 Status | Target Date | Notes |
|--------|---------|-----------|-------------|-------|
| **United States** | T+1 | **Completed** | May 28, 2024 | NSCC clearing fund reduced ~23% ($3B); affirmation rate reached ~95% |
| **Canada** | T+1 | **Completed** | May 27, 2024 | Moved one day before US |
| **India** | T+1 | **Completed** | January 27, 2023 | Pioneer -- first major market to adopt T+1 |

### 3.3 T+0 / Instant Settlement

- **India**: Pioneer in shortened settlement. NSE's NSCCL achieved T+1 for equities in January 2023, making India the first major market. SEBI is now piloting T+0 and instant settlement for select securities.
- **China**: CSDC effectively operates T+1 for A-shares (settlement next day), with some bond products settling T+0. China's pre-funding model ensures settlement certainty.
- **DLT Initiatives**: DTCC's Project Ion processes 100,000+ equity transactions daily on R3 Corda in parallel production; CME is piloting tokenization with Google Cloud Universal Ledger (GCUL); Eurex Clearing launched DLT-enabled collateral mobilization with HQLAx (July 2025).

## 4. DVP Model Comparison

### 4.1 DVP Models in Use

| CCP/CSD | BIS DVP Model | Description | Cash Settlement Medium |
|---------|--------------|-------------|----------------------|
| **DTC** (DTCC) | Model 2 | Gross securities transfers, net funds settlement | Federal Reserve NSS (central bank money) |
| **NSCC/CNS** | Model 2 | Net delivery obligations through DTC, net money | Federal Reserve NSS |
| **FICC-GSD** | Model 1 (Fedwire) | Gross, real-time via Fedwire Securities | Federal Reserve (central bank money) |
| **LCH Ltd** (EquityClear) | Model 3 | Net-net (multilateral net securities + net cash) | PPS (commercial bank money); BoE reserves for GBP |
| **LCH SA** | Model 1 / Model 3 | Depends on CSD/settlement arrangement | Banque de France / TARGET (central bank money for EUR) |
| **OCC** | Via NSCC Accord | Exercise/assignment via NSCC/DTC | Fedwire / commercial bank |
| **CME** | Model 1 (physical delivery) | Gross DVP via Fedwire Securities (for Treasuries) | BMO Harris, JPMorgan, Citibank (commercial bank money); Fed for Treasuries |
| **Eurex Clearing** | Model 1 | Gross DVP via Clearstream/T2S | T2 / TARGET (central bank money for EUR); commercial bank also available |
| **JSCC** | Model 3 | Net securities (JASDEC) + net funds (BOJ-NET/settlement banks) | BOJ-NET (central bank money for JGB); designated settlement banks (commercial) |
| **HKSCC** | Model 2 variant | Net securities, RTGS cash via CHATS | CHATS (RTGS, linked to central bank) |
| **CDP** (Singapore) | Model 3 | DVP through CDP post-trade system | MAS settlement (central bank money) [unverified] |
| **Cboe Clear Europe** | Model 3 | Net-net through 15+ CSDs | Via relevant national CSDs (various) |
| **ASX Clear** | Model 3 | Multilateral net batch via CHESS | RBA (central bank money via RITS) |
| **CSDC** (China) | Model 3 | Net securities + net funds | PBOC / designated banks |
| **CDS** (Canada) | Model 2 | Net securities, net funds via CDSX | Bank of Canada (central bank money) |
| **KRX/KSD** | Model 3 | Net securities (KSD) + net funds (settlement banks) | BOK (central bank money for gov bonds); commercial settlement banks |

### 4.2 Central Bank Money vs Commercial Bank Money

| Settlement Type | CCPs/CSDs Using | Advantages | Disadvantages |
|----------------|----------------|-----------|---------------|
| **Central Bank Money** | DTC (via Fed NSS), FICC (Fedwire), Eurex (T2S/TARGET), JSCC-JGB (BOJ-NET), ASX (RITS), CDS Canada (BoC) | Eliminates commercial bank credit risk; highest safety per PFMI Principle 9 | Limited operating hours; currency-specific |
| **Commercial Bank Money** | LCH Ltd (PPS), CME (settlement banks), CDP [unverified], most cross-border settlements | Greater flexibility; multi-currency; extended hours | Introduces settlement bank credit risk |
| **Hybrid** | Most major CCPs use both depending on product and currency | Balances safety and operational flexibility | More complex to manage |

## 5. Interoperability Map

### 5.1 CCP Interoperability Arrangements

CCP interoperability -- where two or more CCPs clear the same product and maintain mutual risk exposures -- is primarily a European phenomenon.

| CCP 1 | CCP 2 | Products | Venue(s) | Status |
|--------|--------|----------|----------|--------|
| **LCH Ltd** (EquityClear) | **SIX x-clear** | Cash equities | SIX Swiss Exchange | Active |
| **LCH Ltd** (EquityClear) | **Cboe Clear Europe** | Cash equities | Cboe Europe, other MTFs | Active |
| **SIX x-clear** | **Cboe Clear Europe** | Cash equities | Multiple European venues | Active |

**No interoperability links exist for:**
- U.S. CCPs (DTCC, CME, OCC, ICE) -- concentrated domestic structure
- Asian CCPs (JSCC, HKEX clearing houses, CDP) -- domestic monopoly models
- OTC derivatives clearing -- each CCP operates independently

### 5.2 CSD Linkages

| CSD/ICSD | Type | Key Links |
|----------|------|-----------|
| **DTC** (DTCC) | Domestic CSD (U.S.) | Fedwire Securities; operational links with Euroclear Bank, Clearstream, CDS Canada |
| **Euroclear Bank** | ICSD | Bridge with Clearstream; links to 48 domestic markets; T2S (connected Sep 2023) |
| **Clearstream** (CBL/Europe) | ICSD + CSD | Bridge with Euroclear Bank; T2S (50%+ of T2S volume); 60 markets access |
| **T2S** (ECB) | Settlement platform | 24 CSDs from 23 European countries; central bank money settlement |
| **JASDEC** | CSD (Japan) | Links with Euroclear, Clearstream for cross-border settlement |
| **HKSCC/CCASS** | CSD (Hong Kong) | ChinaClear (Stock Connect); Euroclear (Bond Connect) |
| **CSDC/ChinaClear** | CSD (China) | HKSCC (Stock Connect); Euroclear (Bond Connect); expanding global links |
| **KSD** (Korea) | CSD (Korea) | Links with Euroclear, Clearstream, DTC for cross-border settlement |

### 5.3 Cross-Border Clearing Arrangements

| Arrangement | Participants | Description |
|-------------|-------------|-------------|
| **Stock Connect** (Shanghai/Shenzhen-Hong Kong) | HKSCC, ChinaClear | Mutual market access for equities; HKSCC as sole clearing participant of ChinaClear for northbound; ChinaClear as clearing agency participant of HKSCC for southbound |
| **Bond Connect** | CMU (HKMA), CFETS, ChinaClear | Northbound and southbound bond market access; multi-currency settlement (CNY, HKD, USD, EUR) |
| **Swap Connect** | OTC Clear (HKEX), CFETS | Northbound IRS mutual access; launched May 2023; tenor extended to 30 years |
| **CME-FICC Cross-Margining** | CME Clearing, FICC (DTCC) | Capital efficiencies for U.S. Treasury cash and futures positions; launched Jan 2024; customer extension proposed |
| **CME-OCC Cross-Margining** | CME Clearing, OCC | Equity index options (OCC) vs equity index futures (CME); established 1989 |
| **DTCC Cross-Guaranty** | NSCC, FICC, DTC, OCC | Mutual support among DTCC subsidiaries + OCC in member default scenarios |
| **Canton Network** | DTCC, Euroclear, others | DLT-based cross-border tokenization and collateral infrastructure |

## 8. Regulatory Framework Comparison

### 8.1 Regional Regulatory Summary

| Aspect | U.S. | EU | Japan | Hong Kong | Singapore | Australia | Korea |
|--------|------|-----|-------|-----------|-----------|-----------|-------|
| **Primary CCP Regulator** | SEC (securities); CFTC (derivatives) | NCAs + ESMA supervisory college | JFSA | SFC | MAS | ASIC + RBA | FSC / FSS |
| **Systemic Oversight** | FSOC / Federal Reserve (Title VIII) | ESRB / ECB | BOJ | HKMA (CSSO) | MAS (dual role) | RBA (FSS) | BOK |
| **CCP Authorization** | SEC Rule 17A (clearing agency); CFTC Part 39 (DCO) | EMIR Article 14 | FIEA (CCP licensing) | SFO Part III (RCH recognition) | SFA (ACH designation) | Corporations Act (CS facility license) | FSCMA |
| **SIFMU/Systemic Designation** | Yes (8 SIFMUs designated July 2012) | Implicit under EMIR (all authorized CCPs) | JFSA critical FMI designation | No formal SIFMU designation | MAS systemic FMI designation | No formal SIFMU designation | Systemic importance recognized |
| **Clearing Mandate (OTC)** | Yes (Dodd-Frank; IRS, CDS) | Yes (EMIR; IRS, CDS) | Yes (FIEA; JPY IRS, iTraxx Japan CDS) | Yes (SFO Part IIIA; IRS, NDF) | Yes (SFA) | Yes (limited scope) | Yes (limited scope) |
| **Recovery & Resolution** | SEC Rule 17ad-26; Dodd-Frank Title II (FDIC) | EU CCP RRR (Regulation 2021/23, fully applicable Feb 2023) | No dedicated CCP R&R regime; FIEA powers | SFO Division 3 | No dedicated CCP R&R regime | No dedicated CCP R&R legislation | No dedicated CCP R&R regime [unverified] |
| **Settlement Finality** | Federal law (FDICIA, Bankruptcy Code, SIPA, Dodd-Frank) | EU Settlement Finality Directive (98/26/EC) | FIEA; Book-Entry Transfer Act; BOJ Act | SFO Division 3 (market contracts protection) | SFA | Payment Systems and Netting Act 1998 | Capital Market Act |
| **Third-Country CCP Recognition** | CFTC exempt/registered DCO; SEC registered clearing agency | EMIR Article 25 (Tier 1/Tier 2); equivalence decisions | JFSA foreign CCP recognition | SFC recognized clearing house | MAS recognized clearing house | ASIC/RBA foreign CS facility | [data not available] |

### 8.2 CCP Resolution Frameworks Comparison

| Framework | Jurisdiction | Key Features | Applicable CCPs |
|-----------|-------------|-------------|-----------------|
| **Dodd-Frank Title VIII + Title II** | U.S. | SIFMU designation; Federal Reserve backstop lending; FDIC Orderly Liquidation Authority for resolution; SEC Rule 17ad-26 for R&W plans | NSCC, FICC, DTC, OCC, CME, ICE Clear Credit |
| **EU CCP RRR** (Regulation 2021/23) | EU | Mandatory recovery plans; resolution authority designation (NCA); resolution tools (cash calls, VMGH, write-down, position allocation, bridge CCP); fully applicable since Feb 2023 | Eurex Clearing, LCH SA, Cboe Clear Europe, all EU-authorized CCPs |
| **UK framework** | UK | Bank of England as resolution authority; statutory powers under FSMA/Banking Act for CCPs; CBEST cyber resilience testing | LCH Ltd, ICE Clear Europe |
| **Japan** | Japan | No dedicated CCP R&R regime; JFSA uses FIEA enforcement powers (business improvement orders, license revocation) | JSCC |
| **Hong Kong** | Hong Kong | SFC powers under SFO; no dedicated CCP R&R framework | HKSCC, HKCC, SEOCH, OTC Clear |
| **Australia** | Australia | No dedicated CCP resolution legislation; RBA/ASIC coordination under existing Corporations Act and Reserve Bank Act | ASX Clear, ASX Clear (Futures) |

### 10.3 KRX/KSD Positioning

Korea's post-trade infrastructure, centered on KRX (as CCP) and KSD (as CSD), can be benchmarked against global peers across key dimensions:

**Structural Model:**
- KRX operates as an integrated exchange-CCP entity (similar to pre-reform structures), while most Tier 1 peers separate exchange and CCP functions (e.g., JPX/JSCC, HKEX/HKSCC, CME Group/CME Clearing)
- KSD operates as a separate CSD, comparable to JASDEC (Japan), Clearstream (Germany), or HKSCC's depository function
- The KRX-KSD split mirrors the CDP-SGX-DC model in Singapore and the JSCC-JASDEC model in Japan

**Margin Methodology:**
- KRX uses KRX-SPAN (modified SPAN) for listed derivatives -- placing it alongside HKCC (PRiME/SPAN) and ASX Clear (Futures) (SPAN) in the SPAN-based group
- The global trend is moving away from SPAN toward VaR/ES-based methods (CME SPAN 2, JSCC VaR, Eurex Prisma, ICE IRM 2). KRX may consider a similar migration to align with global best practices
- For OTC clearing, KRX uses a VaR-based method, consistent with the global standard

**Settlement Cycle:**
- KRX operates at T+2 for equities, in line with Japan (T+2), Hong Kong (T+2), Singapore (T+2), Australia (T+2), and the EU (T+2)
- The U.S. and Canada moved to T+1 in May 2024; India achieved T+1 in January 2023; China operates at T+1
- Korea is monitoring the global T+1 trend but has not announced a formal transition timeline
- KRX settles government bonds at T+1, comparable to Japan (T+1 for JGBs since May 2018)

**Default Waterfall:**
- KRX's Joint Compensation Fund for derivatives is estimated at ~KRW 100 billion (~$75M), comparable in scale to CDP's S$80M but significantly smaller than Tier 1 CCPs
- KRX places its own SITG contribution in the waterfall before non-defaulting members' resources, consistent with global best practice
- The structure follows the "defaulter pays first" principle, standard across all major CCPs

**OTC Clearing Scope:**
- KRX's OTC clearing scope (KRW IRS, KRW CRS) is narrower than JSCC (JPY IRS + CDS + JGB), LCH (multi-currency IRS + FX + CDS), or CME (multi-currency IRS + FX)
- Expanding OTC clearing mandates and product coverage would align with global trends and G20 commitments

**Technology:**
- KRX uses EXTURE+ (KOSCOM-developed, 2014), an integrated exchange-clearing platform with ~30-50 microsecond latency and 100,000+ TPS. KSD operates dedicated settlement systems with ISO 20022 adoption and SWIFT connectivity. KRX has begun exporting its clearing/settlement technology (Thai Stock Exchange contract, April 2025). KSD's security token mandatory registration framework (effective January 2027) positions Korea as an early mover in DLT-based securities infrastructure.
- Peers are investing heavily in cloud migration (DTCC-AWS, OCC-AWS, CME-Google Cloud, LCH-AWS/Azure, Eurex-Google Cloud) and DLT-based initiatives
- The CHESS replacement failure at ASX (AUD 250M write-off) provides a cautionary example for technology modernization projects

**Regulatory Framework:**
- Korea's FSC/FSS oversight is comparable to Japan's JFSA/BOJ and Hong Kong's SFC/HKMA dual-regulator models
- Korea does not have a dedicated CCP recovery and resolution regime, similar to Japan, Hong Kong, Singapore, and Australia -- unlike the EU (CCP RRR fully applicable since February 2023) and the U.S. (Dodd-Frank Title VIII/Title II)
- Developing a CCP R&R framework would align with FSB Key Attributes and global best practices

**Key Recommendations for KRX/KSD:**
1. **Margin methodology upgrade**: Consider migrating from KRX-SPAN to a VaR/ES-based methodology (following JSCC's 2023 precedent)
2. **T+1 readiness**: Begin industry consultation and system readiness assessment for potential T+1 migration, monitoring UK/EU timelines (2027 target)
3. **OTC clearing expansion**: Evaluate expanding OTC clearing mandates to additional currency pairs and product types
4. **CCP R&R framework**: Advocate for dedicated CCP recovery and resolution legislation
5. **Technology modernization**: Assess cloud migration opportunities and DLT/tokenization pilots for collateral management
6. **Cross-border connectivity**: Leverage existing KSD links with Euroclear/Clearstream/DTC; explore deeper integration with regional CCPs (JSCC, HKSCC) for cross-border clearing arrangements
